title: K8s baremetal bootflow: telemetry, terraform module notes, and rollback plan (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note that combines a suggested bare‑metal boot flow (PXE/iPXE + ignition), instrumentation/telemetry ideas for early‑boot and bootstrap time, Terraform module interface notes, and a pragmatic upgrade + rollback playbook for on‑prem clusters (mixed vSphere + bare metal racks). Goal: reduce mean‑time‑to‑recover for failed bootstraps and make upgrades predictable for staged fleets.

Context / assumptions:
- Customers will run a mix of immutable OS images (custom CoreOS/Ubuntu) or a vSphere VM template alias.
- We expect fleet sizes from 3 node test clusters to 200+ node production clusters across racks.
- Control plane: HA via stacked or external etcd depending on customer preference (we support both).
- Provisioning options: PXE/iPXE for baremetal, OVF/template or cloud-init for vSphere.
- Terraform manages BMC metadata, DNS records, DHCP options, and template registration; not the actual image build (image artifacts stored in S3/minio).

High level boot flow (bare metal):
1) Inventory + BMC -> PXE lease: Terraform writes machine metadata (rack, role, profile, boot-metadata tag) to inventory service.
2) DHCP offers iPXE script that contains a signed ignition URL (short-lived).
3) Node boots kernel+initramfs, mounts ephemeral overlay, fetches ignition by signed presigned URL.
4) Ignition runs to configure kubelet token, kubeadm bootstrap token, and fluent-bit agent for serial logging.
5) Node registers with control plane; cloud-init/ignition writes node labels and annotations (rack, hw-features).

Telemetry / observability during bootstrap (things we lack today):
- Boot timeline histogram (timestamps): first-packet, kernel-loaded, initramfs-exec, ignition-start, ignition-finish, kubelet-start, node-register. Ship as structured events to internal telemetry.
- Serial-console capture: small rolling logs sent via fluent-bit over TLS to a short-lived upload endpoint. Keep only last 10KiB by default; full logs kept behind customer consent.
- dmesg snapshot at ignition completion; include hashed kernel oops signatures to surface reproducible hardware faults.
- PXE server metrics: unknown MAC hits, bad-signed-ignition attempts, missing-image 404s. Alert thresholds: >5% unknown MACs in 10m window for new facility.
- Boot artifacts retention policy: store 7 days by default, 30 days for enterprise.

Terraform module notes (interface sketch):
Module: redwood-onprem-node
Inputs (high level):
- region (string)  -- logical location/rack group
- facility (string) -- human label
- mac_address (string) -- required
- bmc_endpoint (string) -- IP:port for ipmi/redfish
- bmc_creds_id (string) -- secret id for lookup
- boot_profile (string) -- pxeboot|ipxe|vsphere-template
- image_artifact_url (string) -- signed/timestamped image/ignition base
- network_config (map) -- VLAN, MTU, nic-binding
- kube_role (string) -- controlplane|etcd|worker
- taints (list) -- optional
- tags (map)

Outputs:
- node_id (string)
- pxe_boot_url (string)
- ignition_signed_url (string)
- provisioning_status (string)  // created | pending | active | failed

Implementation notes and anti-patterns:
- Avoid long-lived signed URLs for ignition. Use 5–15 minute TTL and a short-step proxy that can inject per-environment secrets.
- Make image_artifact_url optional when using vSphere templates.
- Expose a "reprovision_reason" field so tf plans for reprovisioning carry operator context.

Upgrade plan (control plane + worker) — conservative staged approach:
Preflight checklist (automated where possible):
- Run node inventory checks: kernel version distribution, kubelet version distribution, feature gates, and disk health stats.
- Verify backups: etcd snapshot exists and passes restore dry-run to a sandbox cluster (nightly smoke).
- Validate RBAC & admission webhook compatibility (run static analyzer over manifests).
- Run canary kubeadm upgrade dry-run on single offline node with same OS image.

Staged rollout (recommended):
1) Control plane canary: pick 1 master node in non-HA or 1 AZ for HA clusters. Drain other masters if necessary. Upgrade kubeadm, apply controlplane components, run smoke-tests. If failures -> rollback via etcd snapshot restore (see rollback below).
2) Kubelet & kube-proxy canary on 1–2 workers. Verify perf (cpu/mem), CNI stability, DNS.
3) Rolling upgrade for remainder of controlplane nodes (if HA) with maxUnavailable=1.
4) Rolling upgrade for workers in waves by rack/zone; ensure pod disruption budgets respected.

Canary validation suite (what we run automatically):
- API liveness + response + scheduling test (create replicate, exec, verify cv)
- Job that runs perf microbench (small inference container) to validate latency under core count change
- Networking checks: DNS resolution, CNI mtu path, cross-node connectivity (iperf-lite)

Rollback plan (practical):
- If control plane fails badly (apiserver crashloop, etcd corruption), perform the following:
  a) Promote snapshot: have a fresh etcd snapshot (t-5m ideally).
  b) Boot a temporary control plane with snapshot restore in isolated network (using image with previous k8s version).
  c) Repoint API load balancer to temporary control plane; validate core APIs.
  d) Reprovision remaining masters/workers with previous image/release.
- If single node kubelet upgrade causes regressions: cordon + drain and re-image/rollback kubelet package to previous version and uncordon.
- For boot-level failures (PXE config, ignition malformed): use PXE server to reassign a reprovision tag and reissue new signed ignition; if hardware is flaky, mark node for hardware replacement.

Recovery primitives (we rely on these):
- VM snapshot or disk snapshot (vSphere) for quick revert of templates.
- Full disk images for baremetal stored as artifacts + PXE profile to force reimage.
- Velero or S3-backed etcd snapshots for cluster state.
- Node quarantine flow: place node in maintenance overlay network, redirect telemetry but prevent scheduling.

Troubleshooting checklist (common failure modes):
- PXE never hits: verify DHCP option 66/67 for PXE path and check switch ACLs.
- Ignition 403: TTL expired / clock skew; ensure BMC time sync and check signed URL service logs.
- Kubelet stuck creating container runtime: CRI plugin mismatch or missing CRI systemd unit; check cri.sock presence and permissions.
- Node registers but fails readiness probe: CNI install race - increase kube-proxy/CNI init wait time in ignition.
- etcd high latency: noisy disk or NIC; run fio and collect iostat.

Operational notes and heuristics (from field):
- Prefer reimaging over surgical package downgrades for node-level regressions; images are simpler and more repeatable.
- Try to keep kernel versions within a small window across fleet to avoid driver mismatches.
- For air-gapped/airgapped customers, stage image artifact distribution to local cache and use short-lived local presigners.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical location/format for boot timeline metrics (prometheus histograms vs log events).
- Integrate automated ignition linting into PRs for Terraform modules.
- Add a minimal kubeadm dry-run harness that replays cluster actions in a sandbox using recorded manifests.
- Define retention and access policy for serial logs (privacy/regulatory implications).

Appendix: quick operator recovery play (cheat-sheet)
- Control plane unresponsive: 1) fetch last etcd snapshot ID; 2) allocate small k8s bastion VM with previous-release image; 3) restore snapshot; 4) switch LB; 5) run smoke tests.
- Node stuck in image loop: push new signed ignition for reprovision -> confirm PXE served -> watch serial logs for first 30s; if still failing, mark for out-of-band hw inspection.

Notes to self (short):
- Need to add a diagrams folder for PXE flow and LB failover wiring.
- Link to velero restore playbook and add step-by-step for snapshot verify.

End of doc (WIP)
